title: Toilets, waste and hygiene when plumbing fails
intro: Readings for when toilets cannot be flushed or sewer lines may be broken: emergency toilets, keeping hands clean with little water, handling garbage, and stopping diarrhea from spreading. It also shows the warning signs that mean someone needs medical help.

limits.text: A lot of watery diarrhea in a short time, diarrhea with blood and mucus, or diarrhea lasting weeks are danger signs.
In a cholera outbreak, get people who need it to medical help, such as a field clinic that can give IV fluids.
Dehydration in a child can become serious quickly; if the child does not start to improve quickly with fluids, get help.
If sewer lines are damaged, stop putting toilet, kitchen, shower and bath water into drains until repaired.
Burning plastic or rubber releases toxic chemicals; buried trash with chemicals can contaminate drinking water.
Keep medical waste such as soiled gloves and dressings bagged, marked, and separate from other trash.
Do not build pit toilets on ground that floods, and keep toilets well away from wells, rivers and springs.
